title: Redundant Length Verification Before Safe Collection Get
pattern: Manually checking bounds or size constraints on a collection immediately before calling a safe access API (like `Option` yielding `.get()`) that naturally performs bounds checking internally.
why_bad: It writes redundant branch statements that degrade readability and performance, while duplicating the exact boundaries check already performed at the machine/system library level.
detection: The pattern of checking `index < collection.len()` preceding a safe, non-panicking query of that same element index.
fix: Remove the manual length conditional entirely, allowing the safe library accessor to handle bounds checks natively.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete*, Section 8.1 ("Protecting Your Program from Invalid Inputs") / Section 8.8.
